text:
nina-dx: Noticed a weird combo-breaker this morning: after the SDK moved to a strict exports map + bumped some peer deps, our onboarding playground on Vercel Edge and Cloudflare started failing with runtime + type errors. Minimal repro in the channel.

parker-sdk: Oof. What are the symptoms?

nina-dx: Two things: (1) runtime: `TypeError: sdk.default is not a function` or `import(...).then(...).default is undefined` depending on platform; (2) TS/IDE: no typings resolved, IntelliSense dead. Happens when installing the published package (not from monorepo).

mina-edge: I reproduced on a fresh Next 13 edge app. Steps: `npm i @redwood/sdk@2.0.0` -> start dev -> call server action -> crash.

nina-dx: The publish changed package.json to use exports and also added peerDependencies that bumped the minimal Node to 16.13. But a few CI runners and some customers still run Node 14 in their build step, which seems to affect how bundlers pick entrypoints.

parker-sdk: Can you paste the package.json snippet from the published tarball?

nina-dx: From `npm pack` output of the published artifact:

```
{
  "name": "@redwood/sdk",
  "version": "2.0.0",
  "main": "dist/cjs/index.js",
  "module": "dist/esm/index.mjs",
  "types": "dist/types/index.d.ts",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "dist/esm/index.mjs",
      "require": "dist/cjs/index.js"
    }
  },
  "engines": {
    "node": ">=16.13.0"
  },
  "peerDependencies": {
    "node": ">=16.13.0"
  }
}
```

mina-edge: Important notes: (a) `dist/types` was not actually present in the tarball for 2.0.0 because our build step silently failed for the types emitter. (b) Some edge bundlers (and older Node-run build agents) fall back to `require` resolution; that pulls the CJS build which expects a different shape (exports.default vs named exports), causing the runtime errors.

parker-sdk: Why would build agents pick CJS? Many bundlers consult the `exports` conditional order and platform. If a runner uses an older resolution algorithm or runs an older Node when packaging lambda/edge bundles, it can choose `require`. Also bundlers like esbuild/webpack may prefer CJS if `module` is missing or if package conditions don't include `browser`/`edge`.

leo-build: CI logs show a handful of our self-hosted runners running Node 14 due to an image drift. That explains the inconsistency. The pack script also had `files` omission so types were omitted when the types output step errored.

nina-dx: A twist: onboarding sample imports an auth helper like `import { getAuthToken } from '@redwood/sdk/auth'` using a deep subpath. With the tailored exports map, subpaths were blocked, so the sample failed with `Package subpath './auth' is not defined by "exports"`. We removed deep imports from most code, but samples still do it.

mina-edge: Also noticed subtle retry/auth interplay: CJS build re-exports a wrapper that expects a sync token loader; ESM build supports an async token provider. When the wrong build gets bundled, auth retries fire repeatedly because the token provider shape is wrong -> cascading timeouts in edge functions.

parker-sdk: Ok, concrete action items I propose: 1) Emergency patch 2.0.1 that: includes types in tarball, re-adds permissive subpath exports for `./auth` and a few helpers, and adds an `edge` conditional export that points to `dist/edge/index.mjs`. Example exports shape:

```
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "edge": "dist/edge/index.mjs",
    "import": "dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "dist/cjs/index.js",
    "default": "dist/esm/index.mjs"
  },
  "./auth": "dist/auth/index.mjs",
  "./utils/*": "dist/utils/*.mjs"
}
```

leo-build: Also: add `files` to package.json to force types in tarball and fail publish if types are missing. We'll add an `npm pack` smoke-test in the publish pipeline that runs a minimal `node`/`esbuild` bundle of our sample.

nina-dx: And update our sample apps: stop deep imports, add a note in quickstart about pinning Node to >=16 in build step, and include a small bundler alias snippet for users who hit resolver quirks: e.g., for webpack/esbuild alias to `node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/esm`.

parker-sdk: We should also add an edge-specific integration test in CI that installs the tarball and runs the sample under a clean runtime (simulate Vercel/Cloudflare packing) so we catch resolver differences between Node 14/16 and how bundlers pick entrypoints.

mina-edge: For the auth/retry mismatch it's worth adding a guard at runtime: detect if `tokenProvider` is sync vs async and normalize into an async provider with a migration warning. That would make CJS/ESM mismatches less catastrophic while we patch exporters.

ops-bot: Created issue https://github.com/redwood-repo/sdk/issues/812 and added labels [bug][release-blocker][edge-ci]. Assigned to parker-sdk + leo-build.

parker-sdk: I'll cut the 2.0.1 patch this afternoon with the permissive exports and types fix. Post-patch we remove permissive subpaths in a v3 cleanup after we've migrated all samples and documented the changes.

nina-dx: Thanks — this matches what broke onboarding today. Once the patch lands I'll unpin the sample and re-run the onboarding smoke tests across our edge CI images.
